gloss: older work; previous work; back catalog title

definitions.gloss: older work; previous work; back catalog title
definitions.explanation: A creative work (film, book, album, game, etc.) from an earlier period, as opposed to a new release. Commonly used in entertainment and media contexts to refer to titles no longer considered current.

examples.japanese: {旧作|きゅうさく}のDVDを{借|か}りた。
examples.english: I rented a DVD of an older title.

examples.japanese: レンタルショップでは{旧作|きゅうさく}のほうが{安|やす}い。
examples.english: At the rental shop, older titles are cheaper.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{旧作|きゅうさく}を{全部|ぜんぶ}{読|よ}んでから{新作|しんさく}に{取|と}りかかった。
examples.english: I read all of his previous works before starting on the new one.

examples.japanese: この{監督|かんとく}の{旧作|きゅうさく}は{今|いま}でも{高|たか}く{評価|ひょうか}されている。
examples.english: This director's older works are still highly regarded.

notes:
Composed of {旧|きゅう} (old, former) and {作|さく} (work, production). The direct antonym is {新作|しんさく} (new work/release), and the two are frequently contrasted.

The word is neutral in tone — it simply indicates that a work is not new, without implying that it is outdated or inferior. In fact, {旧作|きゅうさく} is often used when recommending older titles that are worth revisiting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧作|きゅうさく}を{観|み}る: to watch an older film
- {旧作|きゅうさく}レンタル: rental of older titles
- {旧作|きゅうさく}セール: sale on back catalog titles
- {旧作|きゅうさく}も{名作|めいさく}が{多|おお}い: many older works are masterpieces too

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新作|しんさく}: new work, new release — the direct opposite
- {前作|ぜんさく}: previous work — specifically the one immediately before the current one, not older works in general
- {名作|めいさく}: masterpiece — a quality judgment rather than a time-based classification
